title: PPTM to PPTX – Remove Macros from PowerPoint, No Upload
description: Convert a macro-enabled PPTM to a normal PPTX in your browser: the macros are removed without being run, and the slides stay as they were. No upload.
heading: PPTM to PPTX
subtitle: Remove the macros from a macro-enabled PowerPoint file and save it as a normal .pptx; nothing is uploaded.
intro: Convert PPTM to PPTX without PowerPoint: the macros, that is the VBA project and its signature, are taken out of the file and it is saved as a normal .pptx. The macros are never run or read, and the slides, speaker notes and media stay exactly as they were. Macro-enabled templates and shows (.potm, .ppsm) are saved as .pptx too. If a file has no macros, the page says so. Your file never leaves your device.

features.title: Private

features.title: Macros never run

stepsTitle: How to convert PPTM to PPTX

steps.title: Choose your file
steps.text: Click Choose a file, or drop a .pptm, .potm or .ppsm file on the page.

steps.title: Remove the macros
steps.text: The VBA project and its signature are taken out of the file.

handles: Removed: the VBA project and its signature.
Kept: slides, speaker notes, pictures, video and audio.
Result: a normal .pptx file, or a note when the file has no macros.
limits: Buttons and actions that ran macros will do nothing afterwards.
The macros are removed, not kept or shown; this page can't read or convert them.

worksBest: Sharing a deck without its macros

faq.question: Is my file uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Your file is read and changed by your own browser, on your device, and is never sent anywhere. You can check it: open your browser's network panel while you use the tool and you will see no upload.

faq.question: How do I convert PPTM to PPTX?
faq.answer: A .pptm file becomes a .pptx when it is saved again as a PowerPoint Presentation in PowerPoint, which leaves the macros out (checked 24 November 2026). On this page, choose the file and download the .pptx; the macros are removed in your browser without being run.

faq.question: Are the macros run or read?
faq.answer: No. The macros are taken out of the file as they are, without being run or read.

faq.question: What happens to buttons that ran macros?
faq.answer: They stay on the slides but do nothing when clicked, because the macros they called are gone.

faq.question: What if my file has no macros?
faq.answer: The page tells you so; there is nothing to remove.

faq.question: Can I see the slides first?
faq.answer: Yes. Open the file in the PowerPoint viewer; macros are never run there either.

faq.question: Is it really free?
faq.answer: Yes. There is no account, no watermark and no limit on how often you use it.
